newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar and a basket of key foreign currencies on Tuesday in heavy trading by the business sector, dealers said.
On Monday forex trading in Israel was suspended due to a nationwide strike called by the Histadrut labour federation. On Wednesday the market will be closed again for the new year holiday.
"Trading was very active because the business sector was selling foreign currency for end-of-the-year payments," said Israel Sapir of Bank Leumi.
"Other investors were using the opportunity of the rising shekel to buy dollars. The strike had no impact on trading," Sapir added.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2510 shekels against 3.2610 shekels on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6354 shekels against 3.6419 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8031 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8349 on Friday and against the mark at 2.0974 shekels against 2.0983 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.250 shekels.
